findings.text: non-blocking: the fragment says the file 'had read 41 passed in 2.01s before the removal', but the only 41-passed 2.01s log is claude-arm-head.log, whose header names revision 978c8afe — the commit that turned the receipt assertions into absence assertions. No pre-removal run of tests/test_anchored_edit_claude_arm.py is recorded; the worker's own reasoning in resume-1.jsonl calls the base 41-passed a conjecture ('at base (1666d19), these tests assert presence and pass (41 passed)'). The answering commit 040070e41e therefore strengthens the unmeasured claim the prior review flagged rather than measuring it.

non-blocking: the fragment attributes all 23 head failures to 'the worker fence's scheduler shim, which answers sbatch, srun and salloc', but only 6 FAILED lines in importers-run.log carry that text (srun 2, sbatch 2, salloc 2); the rest carry worker-spawn FileNotFoundError, PATH assertions, 'reckon/crew/promotion.py: 50991 estimated tokens exceeds the 50000 bound', an AttributeError on merged_sections and a ValueError. The set comparison establishes the operative claim (head failures are a strict subset of base), so the conclusion stands, but the single-cause explanation is not what the log says.

non-blocking: the manifest's tests line still names tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, and neither file mentions dispatch_launch (grep count 0 in both at 040070e41e), so the gate the record names cannot see a regression of this change; the module-exercising sweep is recorded only under test_logs. This is the prior review's third finding, still unanswered.

non-blocking: at the reviewed head no test fails if the anchored_edit field returns — tests/test_anchored_edit_claude_arm.py, which held the absence assertions, was deleted by the sibling node and the merge took the deletion, and git grep 'anchored_edit' 040070e41e -- tests/ finds only tests/test_anchored_edit.py, tests/test_picker_local_backend.py and tests/test_queue_edit_keeps_the_named_backend.py, none of which asserts the launch record's shape. The fragment states this honestly; the removal is nevertheless unguarded and a regression would land silently.
